subject: maths
title: Primary 1 Multiplication and Division
seo_title: P1 Multiplication and Division Worksheets: Free Primary 1 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Concepts of multiplication and division; use of ×; multiplying within 40; dividing within 20
meta_desc: Free P1 maths worksheets on multiplication and division: equal groups, repeated addition, arrays, sharing and grouping. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Equal groups have the same number in each group. Count the groups, then count one group.
body_html:
Equal groups

Equal groups have the same number in each group. First count the groups. Then count one group.

Repeated addition and ×

We add the same number again and again. We can write it with the × sign. 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4. We say “3 times 4”.

Write it with ×

What is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?

There are four 5s. 4 groups of 5 is 4 × 5. Count: 5, 10, 15, 20.

Answer: 4 × 5 = 20

Arrays

An array puts things in rows. Each row has the same number.

Turn it around and you get 5 rows of 3. It is still 15. So 3 × 5 = 5 × 3.

Sharing equally

Give out the things one at a time until none are left. Every plate gets the same number.

Grouping

Put the things in groups of the same size. Then count the groups.

Grouping

Put 12 counters in groups of 3. How many groups?

Count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 groups.

Answer: 4 groups

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Adding the two numbers (3 × 4 = 7)3 × 4 is 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
Mixing up groups and the number in each group3 groups of 4 is 3 rings with 4 in each ring
Giving one group, not the total (3 groups of 4 = 4)Count all of them: 12
Groups that are not equal (4, 4 and 3)Every group must have the same number
Counting the + signs (5 + 5 + 5 = 2 × 5)Count the 5s: 3 × 5 = 15

faq.q: What multiplication and division is taught in Primary 1?
faq.a: In P1, children learn what multiplication and division mean, using pictures and objects. They multiply within 40 with equal groups, repeated addition and arrays, and divide within 20 by sharing equally and by grouping.

faq.q: Does my P1 child need to memorise multiplication tables?
faq.a: Not yet. The multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 come in Primary 2, so in P1 it is enough to count equal groups and add the same number again and again.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in P1 multiplication?
faq.a: The most common mistake is adding the two numbers, such as 3 × 4 = 7. Ask your child to draw 3 groups of 4 and count them: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics syllabus puts multiplication and division in Primary 1: the ideas of equal groups and sharing, the × sign, multiplying within 40 and dividing within 20.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 3 groups. Each group has 4. Count: 4, 8, 12. So 3 groups of 4 make 12.

items.q: What does the picture show?
items.e: Count the rings: 2 groups. Count one ring: 6 in each. So it is 2 groups of 6. 6 groups of 2 mixes up the groups and the number in each group.

items.q: Which picture shows 2 groups of 5?
items.e: 2 groups of 5 means 2 groups with 5 in each group. C shows this. 5 groups of 2 mixes up the groups and the number in each group. 3 groups of 5 has one group too many. 5 and 4 are not equal groups.

items.q: There are 5 plates. Each plate has 2 curry puffs. How many curry puffs are there?
items.e: 5 groups of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 10 curry puffs. 7 comes from 5 + 2.

items.q: What does the picture show?
items.e: Count the rings: 5 groups. Count one ring: 4 in each. So it is 5 groups of 4. 4 groups of 5 mixes up the groups and the number in each group.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups. Each group has 6. Count: 6, 12. So 2 groups of 6 make 12.

items.q: Are these equal groups?
items.e: Equal groups have the same number in each group. Two groups have 4, but one has 3. So the groups are not equal.

items.q: Which picture shows 3 groups of 4?
items.e: 3 groups of 4 means 3 groups with 4 in each group. C shows this. 4 groups of 3 mixes up the groups and the number in each group. The other pictures have the wrong number of groups or groups that are not equal.

items.q: How many counters are in each group?
items.e: Look at one ring. It has 2 counters. 5 is the number of groups.

items.q: Ali has 3 boxes. Each box has 6 crayons. How many crayons does he have?
items.e: 3 groups of 6: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. 9 comes from 3 + 6. 6 is only one box.

items.q: How many apples are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups. Each group has 5. Count: 5, 10. So 2 groups of 5 make 10.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 3 groups. 6 is the number in each group.
Every group has 5 apples, so the groups are equal. There are 3 groups. It is 3 groups of 5.

items.q: How many apples are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 2. Count: 2, 4, 6, 8. So 4 groups of 2 make 8.

items.q: How many counters are in each group?
items.e: Look at one ring. It has 7 counters. 2 is the number of groups.

items.q: Siti has 4 bags. Each bag has 5 sweets. How many sweets does she have?
items.e: 4 groups of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20. She has 20 sweets. 9 comes from 4 + 5. 5 is only one bag.
There are 5 groups. Each group has 3. Count: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. So 5 groups of 3 make 15.

items.q: What does the picture show?

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 5. Count: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 groups of 5 make 20.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: Count the arrows: 4 jumps of 5. 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20.
Count the 10s: there are 3 of them. So it is 3 groups of 10: 3 × 10 = 30. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: Count the arrows: 5 jumps of 3. 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. So 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: Which is the same as 5 + 5?
items.e: Count the 5s: there are 2 of them. So it is 2 groups of 5: 2 × 5 = 10. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Mei Ling writes 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 30. Which multiplication is the same?
items.e: There are five 6s. That is 5 groups of 6: 5 × 6 = 30. 4 × 6 counts the + signs, not the 6s.

items.q: What is 4 × 5?
items.e: 4 × 5 means 4 groups of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 3 groups of 5. Add 5, 3 times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 + 4 + 4?
items.e: Count the 4s: there are 3 of them. So it is 3 groups of 4: 3 × 4 = 12. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 2. Add 2, 4 times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.

items.q: Which is the same as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2?
items.e: Count the 2s: there are 5 of them. So it is 5 groups of 2: 5 × 2 = 10. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Raju says 3 × 4 = 7. What did he do?
items.e: 3 + 4 = 7. But 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Raju added the two numbers.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?

items.q: What is 2 × 8?
items.e: 2 × 8 means 2 groups of 8: 8 + 8 = 16.

items.q: Which is the same as 6 + 6 + 6 + 6?
items.e: Count the 6s: there are 4 of them. So it is 4 groups of 6: 4 × 6 = 24. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 2 groups of 7. Add 7, 2 times: 7 + 7 = 14.
Turn the dots around. 5 rows of 3 become 3 rows of 5. The number of dots stays the same. So 5 × 3 = 3 × 5 = 15. The answer is 3 × 5.

items.q: This shows 2 × 7 = 14. Which also matches it?
items.e: Turn the dots around. 2 rows of 7 become 7 rows of 2. The number of dots does not change, so 7 × 2 = 14.
Count the rows: 3. Count one row: 7. 3 rows of 7 is 3 × 7 = 21. 3 + 7 only adds the two numbers.
Turn the dots around. 3 rows of 10 become 10 rows of 3. The number of dots stays the same. So 3 × 10 = 10 × 3 = 30. The answer is 10 × 3.
There are 3 rows of 5. Count: 5, 10, 15. So 3 × 5 = 15.
Rows go across. Count down the side: 4 rows. 7 is the number of dots in each row.
Count the rows: 5. Count one row: 8. 5 rows of 8 is 5 × 8 = 40. 5 + 8 only adds the two numbers.
The order can change. The answer stays the same. 5 × 8 = 8 × 5. The missing number is 5. Both make 40.
Count the rows: 4. Count one row: 5. 4 rows of 5 is 4 × 5 = 20. 4 + 5 only adds the two numbers.
Turn the dots around. 2 rows of 9 become 9 rows of 2. The number of dots stays the same. So 2 × 9 = 9 × 2 = 18. The answer is 9 × 2.
Rows go across. Count down the side: 3 rows. 6 is the number of dots in each row.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the dots?
items.e: Count the rows: 2. Count one row: 6. 2 rows of 6 is 2 × 6 = 12. 2 + 6 only adds the two numbers.
The order can change. The answer stays the same. 4 × 6 = 6 × 4. The missing number is 4. Both make 24.
There are 4 rows of 4. Count: 4, 8, 12, 16. So 4 × 4 = 16.

items.q: How many dots are there?
items.e: There are 2 rows of 4. Count: 4, 8. So 2 × 4 = 8.
There are 5 rows of 6. Count: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. So 5 × 6 = 30.
Look along one row: 8 dots. 2 is the number of rows.
Turn the dots around. 4 rows of 7 become 7 rows of 4. The number of dots stays the same. So 4 × 7 = 7 × 4 = 28. The answer is 7 × 4.
Turn the dots around. 3 rows of 5 become 5 rows of 3. The number of dots does not change, so 5 × 3 = 15.
There are 2 rows of 9. Count: 9, 18. So 2 × 9 = 18.

items.q: 15 counters are shared equally on 3 plates. How many are on each plate?
items.e: Count one plate: 5. Check: 3 groups of 5 make 15. So each plate has 5.
Sharing 16 between 2 plates means 2 plates with the same number. C has 8 and 8. 9 and 7 are not equal. 7 and 7 is only 14. 4 plates of 4 has the wrong number of plates.
Share 20 equally into 4 groups. 4 groups of 5 make 20, so each gets 5.

items.q: Mrs Lim shares 10 pencils equally among 5 pupils. How many pencils does each pupil get?
items.e: Share 10 equally into 5 groups. 5 groups of 2 make 10, so each gets 2.

items.q: Share these 8 apples equally on 2 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Give them out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 2 plates gets 4. Check: 2 groups of 4 make 8.

items.q: 14 counters are shared equally. How many are on each plate?
items.e: There are 2 plates. Each plate has 7. 7 + 7 = 14. 2 is the number of plates.

items.q: Hui Min and her friend share 14 stickers equally. How many stickers does each of them get?
items.e: Share 14 equally into 2 groups. 2 groups of 7 make 14, so each gets 7.
Give them out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 3 plates gets 6. Check: 3 groups of 6 make 18.

items.q: Share these 12 counters equally on 3 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Give them out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 3 plates gets 4. Check: 3 groups of 4 make 12.
4 plates of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16. There are 16 apples. 4 is only one plate.
Sharing on 3 plates means 3 plates with the same number. B has 3 plates of 5. 5 plates of 3 has the wrong number of plates. 6, 5 and 4 are not equal. 3 plates of 4 is only 12.
Every plate has 6. So it is an equal share: 18 shared equally on 3 plates is 6 each.

items.q: 18 counters are shared equally on 2 plates. How many are on each plate?
items.e: Count one plate: 9. Check: 2 groups of 9 make 18. So each plate has 9.

items.q: Mr Rahman shares 12 rambutans equally among 3 children. How many rambutans does each child get?
items.e: Share 12 equally into 3 groups. 3 groups of 4 make 12, so each gets 4.

items.q: 12 counters are shared equally on 4 plates. How many are on each plate?
items.e: Count one plate: 3. Check: 4 groups of 3 make 12. So each plate has 3.

items.q: 15 counters are shared equally. How many plates are there?
items.e: Count the plates: 5. Each plate has 3. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 15.

items.q: Share these 15 counters equally on 5 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Give them out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 5 plates gets 3. Check: 5 groups of 3 make 15.
Give them out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 4 plates gets 5. Check: 4 groups of 5 make 20.
Give them out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 2 plates gets 5. Check: 2 groups of 5 make 10.

items.q: Is this an equal share?
items.e: An equal share has the same number on every plate. The plates have 4, 3 and 5. So it is not an equal share. Moving 1 from the plate of 5 to the plate of 3 makes it equal.
5 groups of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. So 5 × 3 = 15. Adding 5 + 3 = 8 is a mistake.

items.q: Which one is sharing?
items.e: Sharing means you know how many groups. “Among 5 children” tells you there are 5 groups. Each child gets 2 sweets.
Make groups of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. That is 5 groups. 16 comes from 20 − 4.

items.q: 12 counters are put in groups of 2. How many groups are there?
items.e: There are 2 in each group. Count the rings: 6 groups. Check: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.

items.q: Hafiz has 15 marbles. He puts 5 marbles in each bag. How many bags does he need?
items.e: Make groups of 5: 5, 10, 15. He needs 3 bags. 5 is the number in each bag.

items.q: On Sports Day, 18 pupils make 3 equal teams. How many pupils are in each team?
items.e: Share 18 equally into 3 teams. 3 groups of 6 make 18, so each team has 6 pupils. 3 is the number of teams.

items.q: Put these 10 counters into groups of 2. How many groups can you make?
items.e: Circle 2 at a time: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 5 groups.

items.q: Wei Ming gets 3 red packets. Each red packet has $5. How much money does he get?
items.e: 3 groups of $5: $5, $10, $15. He gets $15. $8 comes from adding 3 + 5.

items.q: In the canteen, 5 pupils sit at each table. There are 4 tables. How many pupils are there?
items.e: 4 groups of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20. Adding 4 + 5 = 9 is a mistake.

items.q: 20 counters are put in groups of 5. How many groups are there?
items.e: There are 5 in each group. Count the rings: 4 groups. Check: 5, 10, 15, 20.

items.q: Which one is grouping?
items.e: Grouping means you know how many go in each group. “Boxes of 6” tells you there are 6 in each box. 12 eggs make 2 boxes of 6.
Circle 10 at a time: 10, 20. That is 2 groups.

items.q: 16 counters are put in groups of 4. How many groups are there?
items.e: There are 4 in each group. Count the rings: 4 groups. Check: 4, 8, 12, 16.

items.q: There are 7 bicycles at the void deck. Each bicycle has 2 wheels. How many wheels are there?
items.e: 7 groups of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So 7 × 2 = 14. Adding 7 + 2 = 9 is a mistake.

items.q: 18 counters are put in groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: There are 3 in each group. Count the rings: 6 groups. Check: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18.

items.q: Xin Yi puts 3 stickers on each page. She fills 8 pages. How many stickers does she use?

items.e: 4 groups of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40. So 4 × 10 = 40. Adding 4 + 10 = 14 is a mistake.

items.q: Zhi Hao has 5 boxes of mooncakes. Each box has 4 mooncakes. How many mooncakes are there?
items.e: 5 groups of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. So 5 × 4 = 20. Adding 5 + 4 = 9 is a mistake.

items.q: A pencil costs $2. Ethan has $10. How many pencils can he buy?
items.e: Each pencil uses $2. Count in 2s: $2, $4, $6, $8, $10. He can buy 5 pencils.

items.q: A packet has 2 curry puffs. Mrs Ng buys 6 packets. How many curry puffs does she buy?
items.e: 6 groups of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. So 6 × 2 = 12. Adding 6 + 2 = 8 is a mistake.
